questions.question: How should Harsh prioritize preparation for a product-backend role without assuming a particular company's rounds?
questions.answer: This is an editorial preparation plan, not evidence about any company's process. I would first drill the demonstrated gaps: map internals, Streams, SQL, Spring proxies, optimistic locking and cache invalidation. Then practice one coding exercise aloud with edge cases and complexity, followed by a design outline with explicit failure and trade-off discussion. Resume defense needs a concrete connector and incident story without invented internals. Useful starting points are JH-S02-002, JH-S06-007, JH-S07-001, JH-S09-005 and JH-S18-003. The Hot List ranks the current bank, but it cannot predict an employer's exact interview. Rehearsal should alternate explanation, coding and a cold follow-up rather than memorizing paragraphs.

followups.q: How should reported rounds affect this plan?
followups.a: Only after current eligible sources support them; keep reports separate from preparation recommendations.

followups.q: What should be practiced first on a short deadline?
followups.a: The highest-ranked resume-linked GAP or SHAKY questions in L2/L3, followed by an actual coding run.

questions.trap: Presenting a type-level preparation plan as a guaranteed company interview process.
questions.notes: E0 type playbook; linked question IDs are present in this edition.

questions.question: Which backend correctness topics deserve extra attention for a fintech-oriented interview?
questions.answer: As a preparation recommendation, I would emphasize transaction boundaries, idempotency, uncertain outcomes, exact monetary representation, authorization and auditable recovery. The candidate should explain why a timeout is not proof of failure and why broker delivery guarantees do not automatically include a database or payment provider. Starting drills are JH-S07-001, JH-S08-003, JH-S10-002, JH-S11-003 and JH-S13-003. I would connect these to Harsh's real auth and integration work without claiming he built a payment platform. This is not a reported round sequence or a statement that every fintech asks these questions. The interview answer should state the invariant first, then the mechanism and failure recovery.

followups.q: Should the resume claim payment processing experience?
followups.a: No. Discuss transferable auth and integration experience and label payment architecture as a proposed design exercise.

followups.q: What distinguishes a strong answer here?
followups.a: A precise correctness boundary and recovery protocol, not simply naming Kafka, Redis and microservices.

questions.trap: Converting a sensible preparation emphasis into an unsupported claim about a named employer.
questions.notes: E0 type playbook; company-specific round evidence remains separate.

questions.question: How can Harsh keep broad service-role preparation focused rather than memorize a tool list?
questions.answer: I would rehearse a compact foundation in Java contracts, collection choice, Spring wiring, SQL and REST behavior, then prepare a clear account of integration work and release responsibilities. Starting questions are JH-S01-001, JH-S06-001, JH-S09-002, JH-S16-001 and JH-S19-002. For each answer I would explain one mechanism, one practical example and one limitation rather than list every framework used. Role-specific preparation should follow the actual job description and any eligible current interview evidence. This playbook is a type-level recommendation, not a factual list of service-company rounds. Behavioral logistics and client confidentiality still need truthful answers, even when the conversation is mostly technical.

followups.q: Should all service roles be treated alike?
followups.a: No. Client domain, level and project responsibilities vary; use the specific role information when available.

followups.q: How do you answer a tool you only know superficially?
followups.a: State the depth honestly and connect to what you actually used rather than claim production ownership.

questions.trap: Treating a broad company category as evidence for a fixed interview loop.
questions.notes: E0 type playbook; no company names attributed to questions.
